headline: WALL STREET TURNS BEARISH ON GOLD AFTER CPI SHOCK — 85% DEC HIKE ODDS; MAIN STREET STAYS BULLISH
snippet: Friday's October CPI (0.4% month-on-month, above consensus) pushed December Fed rate-hike expectations to approximately 85%, triggering the first majority-bearish swing in Kitco's weekly analyst sentiment survey for 2026. Gold settled below $3,900 as institutional traders repriced rate paths. Main Street retail respondents remained split 2-to-1 bullish, arguing the dip is a buying opportunity before a 2027 policy reversal. The divergence between professional and retail sentiment at the same price level frames the $3,800–$3,900 range as the critical battleground: a weekly close below $3,800 would be the first technical signal that the correction is structural rather than cyclical.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $3,884 SATURDAY AS $3,800 SUPPORT COMES INTO VIEW — SILVER STEADIES NEAR $49
snippet: Spot gold held at $3,884 on Saturday November 14 — up roughly $6 from Friday's close — as markets absorbed the week's CPI-driven selloff. Silver steadied near $49.15 after reaching a one-year low of $48.65 on Friday, with the gold-silver ratio easing slightly from its 78.7 extreme. With U.S. equity markets closed, the weekend price levels represent the clearest read on where physical buyers are willing to hold. October retail sales (Tuesday) and November FOMC minutes (Wednesday) are the two catalysts most likely to either affirm or break the $3,800 support thesis coming into next week.

headline: TUDOR GOLD: 9.00 g/t OVER 9.5m AT TREATY CREEK PERFECTSTORM — 43.29 g/t NESTED HIGH-GRADE SHOOT
snippet: Tudor Gold (TSXV: TUD) reported four new holes at the Perfectstorm Zone on the Treaty Creek property in BC's Golden Triangle: hole PS-26-32 returned 9.00 g/t gold over 9.50 metres, including a nested high-grade shoot of 43.29 g/t Au over 1.20 m down-dip from previously reported surface samples. Companion hole PS-26-34 returned 2.25 g/t Au and 3.10 g/t Ag over 37.50 m, including 10.17 g/t Au over 4.50 m. These are the first holes to test Perfectstorm at depth, confirming the mineralization is not surficial — a material discovery risk removed — and the zone remains open in multiple directions. JV partner Teuton Resources (TSX-V: TUO, 20%) separately confirmed the 2026 season is complete with crews demobilized and 19 PSP Zone assays pending into Q1 2027.

headline: AMERICAS GOLD AND SILVER Q3: RECORD 800,458 oz SILVER — COSALÁ +23%, AISC BLOWS THROUGH GUIDANCE
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX/NYSE American: USAS) produced a company-record 800,458 oz of silver in Q3 2026 — Cosalá's EC120 high-grade zone contributed 415,879 oz, up 23% quarter-on-quarter — but consolidated AISC of $42.94 per silver ounce runs 43% above the $30–$35/oz full-year guidance range. With 2.3 million oz year-to-date against 3.2–3.6 million oz guidance, reaching the low end requires approximately 900,000 oz in Q4. Management says Cosalá's strong cash generation will fund Galena's upgrade program without equity issuance. The report illustrates the two-sided pressure in a correcting silver market: record throughput at the operating level, margin compression at the financial level.

headline: GOLD MINING AISC HITS 13-YEAR HIGH AT $1,930/oz — WGC Q2: CAPEX SURGE COMPRESSES MARGINS 16%
snippet: The World Gold Council's Q2 2026 Gold Demand Trends report reveals that the global all-in sustaining cost for gold mining rose to a record US$1,930 per ounce — up 22% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter — with sustaining capital expenditure hitting an all-time high at $441/oz (up 34% QoQ) and driving a 16% compression in average producer margins even with gold averaging $4,512/oz in Q2. Total cash operating costs of $1,215/oz are also at a record. The WGC notes that absolute cash generation remains strong at current gold prices, but the Q4 correction to $3,884 is now testing the model: at $3,800 gold, the 22% AISC growth rate starts to materially erode the sector's earnings cushion for investors underwriting $4,000+ gold assumptions.

headline: RARE EARTH STOCKS RALLY SECOND SESSION — USAR +3%, MP MATERIALS +2% AS CHINA EXPIRY REFOCUSES WESTERN BUYERS
snippet: The rare earth equity basket extended its recovery for a second straight session on November 13, with Critical Metals rising 3%, USA Rare Earth (USAR) gaining 3% to continue its rebound from its post-earnings crash, and MP Materials (MP) adding 2%. The November 10 expiry of China's rare earth export-control pause — which had temporarily eased Western supply concerns — is now refocusing institutional attention on the limited production alternatives for defence and EV magnet supply chains. MP Materials' commercial GM magnet shipments are expected to begin in Q4 2026, while USA Rare Earth's Serra Verde production ramp remains on track despite Q3 revenue falling far short of analyst models. The two-day rally after the initial sell-off is structurally different from the January 2026 momentum trade: it is driven by supply-chain logic, not momentum.

headline: ZACKS: FURY GOLD, GOLD ROYALTY, NEWMONT, B2GOLD PASS BALANCE SHEET SCREEN FOR SECTOR HEADWINDS
snippet: With gold down 15% in Q2 2026 — its worst quarterly drop in 13 years — and AISC at a record $1,930/oz, Zacks Equity Research screened the mining-gold industry group for names whose balance sheet depth and growth project pipeline can sustain earnings even in a $3,800–$3,900 gold environment. Its November 13 outlook identifies four: Fury Gold Mines, Gold Royalty Corp., Newmont Mining (consensus 2026 EPS estimate up 1.4% over 30 days), and B2Gold. The industry group has gained 10.5% over the past year versus the S&P 500's 11.4% — illustrating the persistent equity discount the sector trades at even when gold sets records — and the current correction is widening that gap further. For self-directed investors, the Zacks framework is a starting screen, not a verdict: balance sheet depth matters, but catalyst timing and cash runway are the variables that will differentiate Q4 performance.

headline: LOTUS RESOURCES FIRST URANIUM SALE FROM KAYELEKERA RESTART — 173,000 LB OFF-SPEC U3O8 TO U.S. BUYER
snippet: Lotus Resources (ASX: LOT) sold approximately 173,000 lb of off-specification uranium ore from its Kayelekera mine in Malawi to a U.S.-listed critical minerals company — the first revenue-generating uranium transaction from the mine since its restart ramp-up. The ore was produced during commissioning at higher-than-specification impurity levels. For the junior uranium sector, the sale confirms that the Kayelekera restart has reached the point of commercial uranium production: at spot uranium of approximately $90/lb, the transaction is worth approximately $15.5 million. With uranium broadly flat over the 30-day corrective period that has hammered gold and copper, the Kayelekera transaction underscores the commodity's independence from broader macro risk-off flows — driven by long-term utility contracting rather than futures sentiment.

headline: MORNING BRIEFING: GOLD AND COPPER AT MULTI-MONTH LOWS — The Sector Technical Damage After CPI Shock
snippet: Mining Stock Daily's November 12 briefing maps the technical damage after gold fell to multi-month lows below $3,900 and copper futures settled at $6.21 — a three-month low — with the Teck Highland Valley strike, macro rate-hike repricing, and a stronger dollar aligning as simultaneous headwinds. The GDXJ (junior gold miners ETF) has fallen disproportionately to gold itself: a 7% correction in spot gold has translated to 20–30% drawdowns for many TSXV-listed names, as operating leverage works identically in reverse. For self-directed investors deciding whether this week's stabilization is a bottom or a pause, the briefing notes that the technical context — few gold miners above their 200-day moving average — is similar to prior corrective phases that resolved with 20–30% recovery rallies within 60–90 days once a credible policy catalyst emerged.

headline: TETHER GOLD RELEASES KPMG AUDIT — RESERVES FULLY BACK TOKEN SUPPLY; PHYSICAL GOLD CUSTODY MARKET MATURES
snippet: Tether Gold (XAUT) released an independent audit by KPMG confirming that its physical gold reserves fully back the outstanding token supply as of November 2026 — the first formal third-party verification the platform has published for some time. For the junior mining investor audience, the story is not about the token: it is about the maturing institutional infrastructure around allocated physical gold. As gold ETFs face redemption pressure from rate-hike expectations, some allocators are evaluating on-chain allocated gold with auditable proof of reserves as a structural alternative — a trend that, if it scales, adds a new category of physical demand that bypasses the futures market entirely and benefits gold producers whose output feeds allocated storage programs.
